source.title: Learning from Teaching Regularization: Generalizable Correlations Should be Easy to Imitate
source.authors: Can Jin; Tong Che; Hong-Wu Peng; Yiyuan Li; Dimitris N. Metaxas; Marco Pavone

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a different explicit regularizer and reports held-out performance against a teacher-only baseline; it does not test the listed claim versions' specific interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses fitting noise-based labels as background, citing prior work; it does not report its own random-label experiment. The student-imitation KL curves compare imitation of sophisticated and deceptive teachers, not train/test classification error gaps or magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.test_reason: The study tests imitability and Learning from Teaching (LoT) regularization, neither of which is a listed claim version. Random-label memorization and dropout benefits appear as background citations. Using dropout or different optimizers in separate workloads does not test their effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: they conclude that generalizable correlations are easier to imitate and that LoT improves performance across tested tasks and architectures. Their efficiency conclusion concerns matched total updates and reported runtime; they also acknowledge added student-training memory and computation.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a jointly trained student and an imitability-feedback regularizer; compares the teacher against a teacher-only baseline.
record.method_sensitivity: LoT performance varies with regularization coefficient α and student steps ratio N; moderate values perform best in the reported PTB LSTM experiments. Student model and architecture combinations also vary across image-classification conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: LoT improves held-out perplexity or accuracy relative to teacher-only training or SFT in the recorded comparisons, with total teacher-plus-student updates matched to baseline updates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Student-feedback regularization can improve held-out performance across the tested language and image tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: In Section 3.1 and Figures 1 and 5, students imitating full-data teachers attain lower training and test imitation KL losses faster than students imitating teachers trained on 2,560 CIFAR-100 examples. Teacher training-set size differs; labels are not randomized.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these teacher comparisons, better-generalizing teachers are easier for fresh students to imitate.

record.problems: The reported classification and language-model results provide held-out metrics but not corresponding training errors or train/test gaps. The study's random-label discussion cites earlier work rather than reporting a random-label experiment.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 has additional teacher/student combinations and ImageNet-1K results; only CIFAR-100 combinations through ViT-B/16 teacher with ViT-B/16 student are represented here. Table 3's remaining rows, Tables 7–13, validation/OOD results, and figure-only sweeps are omitted; these report more held-out performance, efficiency, or auxiliary analyses without measuring the versioned train/test-gap outcomes.

untested.parts: No own experiment comparing fixed random-label fitting and held-out performance with natural-label training under the same recipe.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch, or local-connectivity intervention.
No controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison or tuning-budget comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
No dropout intervention, small-training-set dropout comparison, or joint dropout and weight-decay removal.
No magnitude-aware weight perturbations, sharpness–generalization-gap association, or ranking against norm and margin measures.
No influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples versus equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: None of V1–V8 requires a general train/test-gap measurement as a universal prerequisite. The decisive exclusion is that LoT and imitation KL do not measure the specific interventions or relationships those versions name. All recorded values agree with their cited tables. No omitted result bears directly on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fit or chance-level random-label test accuracy; its own teacher comparison uses different training-set sizes.
No width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks across an interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparison.
Tests Learning from Teaching regularization, not dropout or its interaction with data augmentation and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of generalization-gap measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.
